analysis.title: Hedge Fund VIPs Suffer Worst Day Since 2011 As Two-Thirds Of The S&P Rallies... And The Index Tumbles
key_insights: The S&P fell 1.5% and the Nasdaq 100 fell over 3% on Thursday (Oct 22, 2026) as Meta, Lam Research and Tesla turned an earnings-led stabilization into another AI-capex unwind. 335 S&P members closed higher.

Goldman Prime Brokerage had Fundamental Long/Short funds down 1.1%, Systematic down 1.2% and Multi-Strats down 1.4% as of midday. It was the first time since Covid that all three strategies were down more than 1% on the same day.

Goldman's HF VIP longs vs most-shorted pair (GSTHVIPP) fell about 4.2%, its worst move since 2011, and is down 10.4% month to date. The only larger one-day drop on Bloomberg's chart was -8.26% on August 8, 2011.
Hedge fund short leverage was already near a 5-year high as hedge funds sold tech at a record pace. With crowded longs in AI and crowded shorts in everything else, both legs were hit at once.
US 10Y yields fell about 15bps, the largest one-day move since August 2025. Goldman attributes it to the AI selloff forcing investors to reassess longer-term growth expectations.

Goldman delta-one desk head Rich Privorotsky says AI weakness reprices the capex cycle, takes some pressure off prospective issuance and increasingly becomes a growth shock, so bonds rally when AI sells off.
AI-linked CDS spiked. Meta's credit risk rose on higher spending plans and Tesla's on lower ones. Meta's CDS hit a record and data-center CDS are back at record wides.

The 10Y closed below Goldman's CTA short-term threshold of 5.02% (the level was 5.075% on Oct 16). Medium-term and long-term thresholds are 4.85% and 4.48%. Kaplan expects more bond demand in the next morning's flow estimates.

Goldman's CTA scenario table shows trend followers buying about $18.7 billion of bond futures over the next week and $78 billion over the next month in a flat tape. A 2-standard-deviation rally lifts the week figure to $42 billion.
French 10Y yields topped Treasuries for the first time since 2013 as the French carry trade unwound. Kaplan is watching for flight-to-quality spillover from European rates overnight.
Earnings reactions were constructive on Wednesday, but Meta and Lam Research failed to continue that theme on Thursday. Focus shifts to next week's megacap earnings.
Goldman's AI basket (GSTMTAIP) is down 23% from its June highs, a similar drawdown to the one seen before the July bounce. It is near July's -23.9% trough.
Goldman's High Beta Momentum pair (GSPRHIMO), up about 70% at its June highs, has erased all YTD gains, driven by the AI-correlated long leg.

Across 13 prior one-month GSPRHIMO drawdowns of 10% or more since 2021, the median forward return was +4.77% after a week, +4.20% after a month and +16.41% after three months, with a 77% hit rate at three months. Thursday's -13.65% one-month drawdown is the deepest in the table.
The most recent analog, July 2, 2026, was not an entry point: momentum fell another 15.4% over the following month and 25.8% over six months. March 2026 lost 11.7% over six months.
Goldman's S&P ex-AI index (SPXXAI) has outperformed the S&P by 6% month to date. 45% of S&P names now have negative beta to the index.

Goldman's floor saw 'zero signs of offense' around the AI theme. The floor finished 9.6% better for sale. Asset managers were about 20% better for sale on large-cap tech and ETF supply, and hedge funds 10% better for sale, driven by semis and hardware supply.
Hedge funds showed an uptick in ETF shorting, with shorts outpacing long sales 2:1.

155 S&P names had moves of 2.0 sigma or more, the highest since the May 2025 US-China tariff truce, while 335 names closed higher, one of the widest gaps between breadth and index performance since the 1990s. The biggest movers were Allegion (+11%), Roper (+9.7%), General Mills (+8%), Nasdaq Inc. (+7.5%), CSX (+6.8%), American Water Works (+6.3%) and Procter & Gamble (+5.6%).

The author argues the bulls have a case (AI basket at July's low drawdown, momentum crashes historically good entries, Treasuries hedging again, ex-AI index strong) but is skeptical. The trigger came from credit and funding, which positioning washouts do not fix. The author says the dip may need more time and next week's megacap earnings will show whether July's bounce repeats.

market_movers.rationale: Meta went from AI savior to poster child for negative FCF overnight. Its CDS hit a record on higher spending plans and it failed to extend Wednesday's constructive earnings reaction.
Lam Research failed to continue the constructive earnings reaction seen Wednesday and was named among the names driving the Nasdaq 100 decline.
Tesla was named among the names driving the AI-capex unwind. Its credit risk rose on lower spending plans.
Allegion rose 11% on Thursday, the largest two-sigma mover in the S&P.
Roper rose 9.7% on Thursday as part of a defensive and non-AI rally.
General Mills rose 8% on Thursday as part of a defensive rally with little desk rotation behind it.

sector_views.rationale: Hedge funds and asset managers were sellers of large-cap tech, semis and hardware, and the AI basket is down 23% from its June highs.
These sectors rallied Thursday, but Goldman's desk saw little active rotation into them, so the moves reflect light positioning rather than new demand.

earnings_insights: Wednesday (Oct 21) tech earnings reactions were constructive per Goldman's Kaplan, but Meta and Lam Research (reported results, reaction on Thursday Oct 22) failed to continue that theme.
Next week's megacap earnings are the next test of whether July's bounce repeats. No consensus figures are given.

macro_indicators.reading: Down about 15bps on the day, back below 5%
macro_indicators.interpretation: Largest one-day move since August 2025. It reflects a flight to quality and growth repricing as the AI selloff continues.
The 10Y closed below the trigger, which Goldman expects to bring trend-following bond demand. The next trigger is 4.85% and the long-term trigger is 4.48%.
First time since 2013, tied to the French carry trade unwinding and a possible source of European flight-to-quality spillover.

risk_factors: Funding and credit stress in AI: Meta's CDS at a record and data-center CDS at record wides, which positioning washouts do not fix.
Crowded positioning in AI longs and everything-else shorts hits both sides of hedge fund books at once.
Momentum dip-buying has been unreliable recently, with July 2026 and March 2026 both followed by further losses.
European rates spillover, including French yields above Treasuries.
Next week's megacap earnings could extend or reverse the AI unwind.
Liquidity draining in the selloff could lead to solvency concerns.

tension_points.bull_case: The AI basket is at the same 23% drawdown that marked July's low, momentum crashes have historically been good entries (77% hit rate at 3 months, median +16.41%), Treasuries are hedging again with CTAs buying, and the S&P ex-AI index is outperforming.
tension_points.bear_case: The July 2 analog lost another 15.4% over the following month. The trigger this time is credit, with AI CDS and Meta CDS at records, and positioning washouts do not fix funding problems.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Next week's megacap earnings: a repeat of July's bounce would support the bulls, further AI credit widening would support the bears.
